acceptance_criteria: tests/test_docs.py's predicate is quoted verbatim and its reach stated before any name is written.
The attribution is derived from commit trailers with counts, or the weakness is stated.
README carries scope, what-it-is, provenance and dual-nature, each present.
The measured live result and its limits appear side by side.
No serving model is named in README.md — asserted.
Any contradiction with a measured fact is named rather than silently corrected.
Suite passes; count reported before and after.
assumptions: The development roster the owner names (a DeepSeek model as architect; Claude and Muse agents as coders) appears in the commit trailers. If it does not, the credit must be narrowed to what the history shows.
constraints: FIRST, READ THE GUARD. Quote tests/test_docs.py's predicate verbatim and state exactly what it scans for and in which files. Do not write a model or agent name into README.md until this is answered. If the guard cannot distinguish a development-agent name from a serving-model name, say so and return the question rather than guessing.

SECOND, VERIFY THE ATTRIBUTION against the repo, not against this command. Run git log and report the actual trailers and Co-authored-by lines across the project, with counts. The README credits what the trailers say. If a named agent has no trailer, say so — the README must not assert a provenance the history does not carry.

THE ATTRIBUTION IS A CLAIM ABOUT THE REPO and is therefore generated or guarded (convention 24). If the trailer evidence is weak or ambiguous, state that plainly and recommend a narrower wording rather than a fuller claim.

THE README CARRIES FOUR THINGS: (1) SCOPE — what the harness is for, what it produces, and what it explicitly does not do; (2) WHAT IT IS — a working multi-model agentic harness for engineering R&D, six workflows, that reaches a terminal on a live run; (3) PROVENANCE — the development roster credited as the trailers record it, and that the project was built by agents operating under a protocol; (4) THE DUAL NATURE — that it is both a working program and a worked directory of how agents and LLMs can produce one, with the channel, the ledger and the conventions as the evidence.

DO NOT CLAIM MORE THAN IS TRUE, and this applies hardest to the dual-nature section. State the measured result: one live completed run, 9 calls, $0.06, validate 6/6, review ship:true. State the limits beside it: quality is measured as termination, not correctness; six tiers require configuration; auth is open by default. A README that reads as a finished product will be found out by the first user.
DO NOT name a serving model in README.md. The provenance credit names development agents; the serving roster is the operator's and belongs in HANDOVER.md §6 and the ledger.

Do NOT restructure the existing README. Add the scope and provenance sections; leave what is there unless it contradicts a measured fact, and if it does, name the contradiction rather than silently correcting it.
Keep the diff small. Suite reported before and after.

questions: Does tests/test_docs.py distinguish a development-agent name from a serving-model name, or does it scan for a flat token list? This decides whether the credit line can name agents at all, and it is the first thing to check.

Is the README credit intended to name the models or the agent roles? 'Architect' and 'coder' are roles; the models are implementation detail. Naming roles would sidestep the guard entirely and is arguably the more durable claim — state a preference.
rollback: Revert the commit; README returns to its previous text.
